introduction.en: The Eight Core Sectors—Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, and Electricity—constitute 40.27% of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP). They are considered the backbone of the industrial sector.
introduction.hi: The Eight Core Sectors—Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, and Electricity—constitute 40.27% of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP). They are considered the backbone of the industrial sector.

body.en: These sectors are vital because they provide the essential inputs for other industries. For instance, steel and cement are critical for infrastructure, while electricity and coal drive manufacturing. Their performance acts as a lead indicator, signaling the health of the broader economy. A contraction in these sectors often precedes a slowdown in the overall industrial output.

conclusion.en: Given their multiplier effect, sustained growth in these sectors is essential for achieving the goal of a $5 trillion economy and strengthening India's manufacturing base.
